summary: 58-year-old man seen with the histology of an 18 mm polyp removed at colonoscopy for a positive FIT.

inputs.hpi: Colonoscopy for a positive FIT (FIT 32 µg Hb/g): one 18 mm pedunculated sigmoid polyp removed en bloc; rest of the colon normal to the caecum. No bleeding, no change in bowel habit, no weight loss.

imaging.name: Histology: sigmoid polyp
imaging.result: Tubulovillous adenoma with low-grade dysplasia, 18 mm, completely excised (margin clear). No invasive malignancy.

mustRankTopK.note: The pathology is the diagnosis; the vademecum offers it to the outcomes loop as a final-diagnosis prompt (never written without the clinician).
mustRankTopK.knownGapNote: Web PANE (2026-09-26): no adenoma diagnosis in PANE and the histology report is not read; the vademecum shadow treats the histology as definitive and prompts a final diagnosis.

guideline.name: BSG/ACPGBI/PHE post-polypectomy and post-colorectal cancer resection surveillance guidelines
guideline.section: High-risk findings (≥ 2 premalignant polyps including ≥ 1 advanced, or ≥ 5 premalignant polyps): one-off surveillance colonoscopy at 3 years; otherwise no colonoscopic surveillance (return to screening). A single completely excised advanced adenoma is not high risk on its own.

rationale: Entry point: pathology. Confirmation rather than hypothesis: the vademecum treats the histology as a definitive (pathognomonic) finding and prompts a final diagnosis for the outcomes loop.

authoring.author: Claude (vademecum phase 1, entry-point pilot)
authoring.notes: Starts from a result (laboratory, imaging or pathology), not a complaint. Written for the vademecum shadow (clinval:web --engine vademecum); not verified on iOS; clinical sign-off pending (docs/clinical-validation/changes/vademecum-phase1.md).
